committee_name.text: Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee

quote.quote: The Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee of the Food and Drug Administration met on December 5, 2008 at the Hilton Washington/Rockville 1750 Rockville Pike, Rockville, Maryland.
Besifloxacin was presented to the FDA's Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Advisory Committee on December 5, 2008.

recommendation.text: The committee voted unanimously (Yes 9; No 0) in favor of approval of besifloxacin for the treatment of bacterial conjunctivitis.

quote.quote: The Committee voted unanimously (Yes 9; No 0) in favor of approval of besifloxacin for the treatment of bacterial conjunctivitis.

summary: The Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee met on December 5, 2008 and voted unanimously (9-0) to recommend approval of besifloxacin (Besivance) for bacterial conjunctivitis, agreeing that safety and efficacy were demonstrated. The committee suggested adding labeling language for use in patients with pre-existing dry eye and other corneal surface conditions, but that language does not appear in the approved label (the WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS section lists only Topical Ophthalmic Use Only, Growth of Resistant Organisms, and Avoidance of Contact Lenses), so no AdComm concern can be verifiably tied to a change in the approval. The notable approval decisions (7-day vs 5-day labeled treatment duration and the postmarketing safety requirement) were driven by internal FDA/OND discussion rather than the advisory committee, so no AdComm-to-change linkages are reported.
